subject: Feasibility sync: Autumn Health pilot (VPC / on‑prem) — architecture & exception path

To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Anna Reynolds <anna.reynolds@autumnhealth.com>, Paul Owens <paul.owens@autumnhealth.com>
Cc: Legal <legal@autumnhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Feasibility sync: Autumn Health pilot (VPC / on‑prem) — architecture & exception path

Team / Anna & Paul —

Thanks for taking time to kick off the feasibility conversation. Autumn Health is proposing a pilot that requires either a private VPC deployment in their AWS account or a small on‑prem appliance inside their data center. Highlights from their requirements (attached):

- Customer must retain full control of data at rest and in transit; keys managed in their KMS.
- No outbound telemetry to our hosted control plane for model payloads (control plane calls for ops metadata okay with logging consent).
- Pilot scope: ~5k inference requests/day, peak burst to 200 concurrent sessions, 2–3 models (1 LLM + 2 rerank/embeddings).
- Required SLA: 99.5 availability for the pilot window; audit logs for all admin actions.

Primary asks for internal alignment:
1) Architecture feasibility: is our private control plane + on‑prem runtime able to satisfy the no‑egress requirement without a long re‑architecture?
2) Security gating: what exact evidence (SOC2, KMS integration, HSM) do we need to present, and where do exceptions fit?
3) Resource runway: estimated staffing and timeline for a pilot like this (minimal viable runway).

Can each function reply with a short assessment and 1–2 concrete asks (e.g., "need X days and Y FTEs", "need exception for outbound telemetry for control plane"), so I can consolidate and get back to Autumn Health by EOD Monday.

Attachments: autumn_pilot_requirements.pdf

Thanks —
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Anna Reynolds <anna.reynolds@autumnhealth.com>, Paul Owens <paul.owens@autumnhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feasibility sync: Autumn Health pilot (VPC / on‑prem) — architecture & exception path

Sergio / all —

Quick technical read: the runtime can be delivered in two basic patterns but each has tradeoffs. Short answers below, followed by concrete asks.

Options:
- Private VPC in customer account: feasible with our private control plane offering. Requires cross‑account IAM roles, NAT rules to prevent egress for model payloads, and a private peering/endpoint for control plane telemetry. Works with their KMS for key wrapping.
- On‑prem appliance: feasible but heavier. We need either baremetal Linux + CUDA nodes or an airgapped container host plus a minimal management agent. More ops overhead.

Gating constraints and asks from infra/arch:
1) Network: we need a customer VPC peering design template and a one‑page network ACL checklist from the customer (we can provide).
2) Model runtime: confirm model sizes — if they want a 70B model we need quantization guidance; 3–4x more memory. For pilot assume a 13–34B model to keep the hardware footprint reasonable.
3) Ops: request 4 weeks to stand up POC infra once we have the VPC/VPN connectivity and KMS config. Need 1 infra engineer (0.5 FTE) and 1 runtime engineer (0.5 FTE) dedicated during that window.

Ask to the customer (Anna/Paul): can you confirm target model family (size) and whether you have an HSM-backed key policy already? That will materially affect timeline.

Thanks —
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Architect, Runtime

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Anna Reynolds <anna.reynolds@autumnhealth.com>, Paul Owens <paul.owens@autumnhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feasibility sync: Autumn Health pilot (VPC / on‑prem) — architecture & exception path

Sergio / team / Anna & Paul —

From a security & compliance standpoint we can support this pilot, but there are clear evidence and architectural gating items. I attached a checklist with the minimum artifacts we need. High level:

- Mandatory: SOC2 Type II report, documented KMS/HSM integration (key rotation policy), formal network segmentation diagram, and admin audit log retention policy.
- Strongly recommended: endpoint scanning and host‑level EDR on on‑prem hosts; VPN configuration that avoids split tunneling; signed attestation for any third‑party drivers.
- Exception lane: if the customer cannot provide outbound telemetry due to policy, we can allow a restricted control plane connection only for heartbeat/health and operational traces, but we must document the exception and limit retention (30 days) and require an explicit legal addendum.

Concrete asks from Security (to move forward):
1) Customer to provide SOC2 summary and contacts for their compliance officer (timeline: 3 business days).
2) If customer requires no outbound telemetry at all, Legal needs to prepare an exception addendum and Security needs a weekly oncall window with customer ops for incident response.
3) We will need to run a short on‑prem penetration sanity test (3 days) before SLA kickoff.

Attachment: security-evidence-checklist.xlsx

Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Anna Reynolds <anna.reynolds@autumnhealth.com>, Paul Owens <paul.owens@autumnhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feasibility sync: Autumn Health pilot (VPC / on‑prem) — architecture & exception path

Sergio / team —

Operationally, here are the staffing and timeline assumptions for a minimal viable pilot (goal: production‑grade but limited scope).

Proposed runway & roles (concurrent):
- Week 0–2: Requirements + network connectivity (Customer + Karthik)
- Week 3–6: Infra + runtime deployment (1 infra engineer 0.5 FTE, 1 runtime engineer 1.0 FTE)
- Week 6–10: Hardening, pen test, smoke, and pilot ramp (1 SRE 0.5 FTE, CS engineer 0.5 FTE for onboarding)

Staffing ask: dedicate 2.5 FTEs spread across 6 weeks (counts above as fractional). Budget: assuming internal blended rates, estimate ~USD 85k for the pilot ramp (infrastructure + engineering hours). If we require an on‑prem appliance with larger model sizes (>=34B), add another 1.0 FTE for hardware ops and extend runway by 3 weeks.

Dependencies / open items:
- Karthik: confirm model family/size.
- Kimberly: confirm whether exception lane is acceptable and what Legal language is required.
- Anna/Paul: provide SOC2 summary and KMS/HSM contact.

Attachment: pilot-staffing-asks.md

Marissa Cole
Head of Product Operations

- Karthik to produce a 1‑page VPC peering + ACL template and a short runbook for zero‑egress configuration — due Fri 2026‑10‑16 — owner: Karthik Iyer.

I will draft a single project summary for Autumn Health that includes the above asks, an estimated runway (6–10 weeks depending on model size), and the exception path if needed. I'll share the draft in the Drive folder and propose a follow‑up call next Thu to lock the pilot kickoff.
